source.initial_construction: Existing typed GraphBuilder/Proc and program_store, full verify_store and Workspace.save. Canonical graph is authoritative; external construction carrier is not maintained source.

contract.stdin: Read raw bytes to EOF, at most 65536. Reject excess before calling the decision. Fragmented reads and EINTR retry.
contract.decision: Existing borrowed initialized input/output/tape views of 65536 bytes each, explicit full-reset core, logical input length and output capacity 65536; typed direct call, no interpreter.
contract.stdout: Check success and returned length <=65536 before writing. Write the complete successful output, retrying partial writes/EINTR; discard language-failure output prefixes.

exit.5: read/write failure or invalid returned output length

contract.allocation: Three distinct owned zero-initialized 65536-byte mmap views, released with munmap; checked-null allocation failure traps. Declared views are not RSS.
contract.target: Existing aarch64-linux-elf-exec-v1 static ELF with explicit Linux AArch64 syscalls, executed on Android ARM64. No dynamic loader, libc or runtime; no desktop Linux delivery/benchmark claim.
contract.entry: Proof-only entry parameters and explicit exit_group; no command-line options.
contract.source_purity: No BBC source or BFX byte change. All new executable implementation is canonical XAX graphs; unchanged Python bootstrap APIs verify/lower/package.

transport_diagnosis: Direct ADB shell output translated LF to CRLF; exec-out did not forward stdin EOF on this host. Functional binary I/O therefore uses redirected remote files and pull, plus a native pipe timer.

Shell fd redirection did not provide a reliable closed stdin and /dev/full was inaccessible. A separate native fd-closing exec transport checks actual EBADF on stdin/stdout. No production graph change was needed.
limitations: Twelve fixed workloads and only three process clusters, with uncontrolled clocks/affinity/thermals.
No best-mode sweep, full source-profile equivalence against the comparators, 20-workload/three-application gate, steady-state comparator timing, compiler latency, RAM or Windows standalone result.
Awib process advantage applies only to this pinned configuration, common safe no-EOF subset, tested Pixel and process boundary. No compiler is unrestrictedly SURPASSED.
Brainfry process aggregate remains faster. Existing build-cost and Windows comparisons retain their original evidence.
Allocation-failure, syscall EINTR and forced short-write fault injection were not performed; fragmented reads, descriptor failures and large file/pipe output were executed.
